title: 받아쓰기 2: 예사소리·거센소리·된소리
objective: Tell plain, aspirated and tense consonants apart, and write them when you hear easy words.
summary: Practice hearing and writing plain, aspirated and tense Korean consonants.

task.title: Listen and write
task.line: Read the sound in quotes (or listen to your teacher), then choose or write the right Hangul.

letters.sound: Plain [g/k] soft; aspirated [kʰ] with air; tense [k͈] tight, no air.
letters.as: g in 'go' / k in 'kite' / k in 'sky'

letters.sound: Plain [d/t] soft; aspirated [tʰ] with air; tense [t͈] tight, no air.
letters.as: d in 'day' / t in 'top' / t in 'stay'

letters.sound: Plain [b/p] soft; aspirated [pʰ] with air; tense [p͈] tight, no air.
letters.as: b in 'boy' / p in 'pie' / p in 'spy'

exercises: Circle the syllable that matches the sound: ① "kkae" 개 / 캐 / 깨 ② "tal" 달 / 탈 / 딸 ③ "bul" 불 / 풀 / 뿔
Add ㄱ, ㅋ, or ㄲ to finish the word: ① _ㅓ피 (keopi, coffee) ② 토_ㅣ (tokki, rabbit) ③ _ㅏ방 (gabang, bag)
Write the word in Hangul: ① bada (sea) ② podo (grapes) ③ appa (dad)
Write the sentence in Hangul: ① Kiga keoyo. (He is tall.) ② Aiga jayo. (The child is sleeping.) ③ Bappayo. (I'm busy.)
answers: ① 깨 ② 탈 ③ 불
① 커피 ② 토끼 ③ 가방
① 바다 ② 포도 ③ 아빠
① 키가 커요. ② 아이가 자요. ③ 바빠요.
